title: Discrete distributions are learnable from metastable samples
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75439-1

Algorithms sampling from thermal states of many-body systems often get stuck in restricted, metastable states. Here, authors prove that the true underlying models can nevertheless be accurately recovered from these trapped samples, establishing rigorous learning guarantees for discrete distributions.

title: Concept2Brain: an AI model for predicting neurophysiological responses to text and pictures
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75653-x

Advancing toward human brain simulation remains a major challenge. Here, the authors introduce Concept2Brain, an AI web tool that predicts neural activity, thus generating synthetic and reproducible EEG datasets from text or picture inputs.

title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals distinct cell type dynamics following opioid dependence in female mice with the common human μ-opioid receptor variant Oprm1 A118G
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75723-0

Gene expression mapping in mice reveals how genetic risk for opioid dependence shapes transcriptional architecture of the brain. Here authors show that the Oprm1 risk allele (G) links to glial changes, while the protective allele (A) promotes neuronal plasticity.

title: Dyscoordination of thalamic reticular spindles is associated with social memory deficits in mice and humans with autism spectrum disorder
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75162-x

The relationship between sleep spindles and social memory is not fully understood. Here authors identify a thalamic sleep spindle circuit that supports social memory consolidation and is disrupted in autism. Restoring spindle activity rescued social deficits in mice, and spindle features predicted autism in children.

title: Deletion of ARPKD-associated Pkhd1 gene in mice results in decreased Tfap2b expression and eye abnormalities
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75698-y

Genetic studies have linked the PKHD1–TFAP2B locus to glaucoma risk, but the underlying mechanism is unclear. Here, the authors show that deleting Pkhd1 in mice disrupts Tfap2b regulation in developing eye tissues, causing congenital glaucoma-like defects and implicating TFAP2B dysregulation in disease risk.

title: A hierarchical framework for cortical and subcortical gray-matter parcellation across rodents, primates, and humans
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75837-5

Researchers built a unified atlas that maps matching gray-matter regions across mouse, rat, marmoset, macaque, and human, enabling direct cross-species comparison and revealing conserved sensorimotor but divergent association-cortex organization.

title: RHOT1/2-driven mitochondrial membrane vesicles confer tumor-homing selectivity and enable in situ cancer vaccination
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75830-y

The development of effective immune reactive cancer therapies has been constrained by the lack of delivery systems with precise tumor selectivity. This study leverages an RHOT1/2- mediated fibroblast mitochondrial transfer mechanism to enable tumor-specific uptake within a gold-based nanoplatform, inducing durable antitumor immunity.

title: Dual-space visible light authentication toward high security physical unclonable function
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75781-4

Real and reciprocal space visible signals from polycrystalline self-assembly constitute high security optical keys for straightforward authentication that overcomes inherent counterbalance between authentication efficiency against security level.
